You are going to turn a recipe into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme recipe and deliver a live timeline: Backyard Barbecue: Smoker and Grill for a shoulder, sausages and sides for about twelve
Resource limits: one offset smoker, one kettle grill, one side burner, one cooler for holding, two cooks.
No finishing time was given; finish as early as the work allows.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Backyard Barbecue: Smoker and Grill

Two cooks, one offset smoker, one kettle grill, one side burner and a cooler for holding. The pork owns the smoker all day; everything else happens in the last two hours.

Pork shoulder
Light the smoker and bring it to 250°F; 45 minutes. While it comes up, trim the shoulder and rub it heavily with salt, pepper and paprika; 25 minutes. Put the shoulder on once the smoker holds temperature and smoke it unwrapped for 6 hours, until the bark is dark and set. Wrap it tightly in butcher paper; 10 minutes. Back on the smoker, wrapped, until the thickest part probes soft — usually another 3 hours, sometimes four. Hold it wrapped in a cooler for one to three hours; it will not get cold and it only gets better. Pull the meat by hand; 30 minutes.

Beans
When the pork goes into the cooler, fry the bacon and onion in the pot on the side burner for 12 minutes, then add the beans, molasses and a ladle of drippings and let them tick over on the lowest flame until you serve.

Slaw
Start the slaw at the same time. Shred the cabbage and carrot; 20 minutes. Whisk the buttermilk dressing; 8 minutes. Dress the slaw and put it in the refrigerator for at least 45 minutes so the cabbage softens.

Grill
Light the kettle an hour before you eat; 25 minutes to a clean bed of coals. Grill the sausages for 14 minutes. Grill the corn for 10 minutes. Toast the buns for 3 minutes, last, so they stay warm.

Table
Set out plates, pickles and sauce once the buns are off; 10 minutes. Call everyone over when both cooks say it is ready; 5 minutes to lay it all out.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. This is a backyard barbecue for about twelve people, built around a single pork shoulder that occupies the smoker essentially all day: light and stabilize the smoker (45 min) while trimming and rubbing the shoulder (25 min), smoke it unwrapped for 6 hours, wrap it in butcher paper (10 min), smoke it wrapped for another 3–4 hours until probe-tender, then rest it wrapped in a cooler for 1–3 hours before pulling the meat by hand (30 min). Everything else — beans, slaw, and the grill work for sausages, corn and buns — is compressed into roughly the last two hours before serving: beans start (bacon/onion 12 min, then simmer indefinitely until serving) the moment the pork goes into the cooler; slaw (shred 20 min, dress 8 min, then a minimum 45-minute chill) starts at the same time; the kettle grill is lit about an hour before eating (25 min to good coals) and used sequentially for sausages (14 min), corn (10 min), and buns last (3 min) so they stay warm; the table is set once the buns are off (10 min), and everyone is called over for a final 5-minute plating once both cooks agree it's ready. No explicit deadline/finish time was given, so the schedule should be arranged to finish as early as the dependency chain allows. Equipment/people constraints are singular and binding: one offset smoker, one kettle grill, one side burner, one cooler, and only two cooks to run all of it, so the smoker-track work and the last-two-hours side/grill work must be coordinated around those shared single resources and the two available cooks.

completion.text:
**Restating the model:** A track is a single lane of sequential work — the pork, the beans, the slaw, and the grill/table each form their own track because they happen concurrently, and within any one track a step cannot start until the previous step in that track has ended. Each step carries exactly one kind of duration: `fixed` when the time is known (a 45-minute smoker light, a 20-minute chop), `variable` when the source gives a range (the 3–4 hour wrapped smoke, the 1–3 hour cooler hold), or `indefinite` when it just runs until someone stops it (the beans "ticking over until you serve"). A `startTrigger` is what actually schedules a step against the clock or against another step's finish (or start, with an offset/buffer) — `programStart` for the very first things, `afterStep`/`afterStepWithBuffer` for "once the previous thing is done (plus some gap)," `programStartOffset` for "an hour before the rest," and `manual`/`compound` for human judgment calls like "when both cooks agree it's ready." `stepId`s must be unique across the entire program since triggers can reach across tracks (e.g., beans starting when the pork goes into the cooler). Finally, any physical thing only one of which exists — the smoker, the kettle grill, the side burner, the cooler — needs a `resourceConstraints` entry with `maxConcurrent` set to how many steps can actually occupy it at once, which is what will stop the runner from, say, trying to grill sausages and toast buns on the kettle at the same instant; since this recipe has no repeated identical work item (one shoulder, one batch of beans, one batch of slaw), I don't expect to need `replicates` here.

**Expected resource constraints for this recipe:**
- smoker — used almost the whole day by the pork (light, unwrapped smoke, wrapped smoke); only one exists.
- grill (kettle) — used sequentially for lighting, sausages, corn, buns; only one exists.
- burner (side burner) — used for the beans (fry, then indefinite simmer); only one exists.
- cooler — used once, to hold the wrapped pork; only one exists.
- prep — hands-on work (trimming/rubbing, wrapping, pulling, shredding, dressing, table-setting, plating) done by the two cooks; capped at 2 concurrent since that's the whole crew.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "A track is one sequential lane of work with no overlap between its own steps; concurrent activities (pork, beans, slaw, grill/table) go in separate tracks. Each step has exactly one duration kind (fixed/variable/indefinite) and one startTrigger that anchors it to the program clock or to another step's start/end, possibly with an offset or buffer, or to a manual/compound decision. stepIds are unique across the whole program because triggers can reference steps in other tracks. Every task a step occupies (smoker, grill, burner, cooler, prep) needs a matching resourceConstraints entry whose maxConcurrent enforces the real-world limit of one smoker, one grill, one burner, one cooler and two cooks. This recipe has no repeated identical work item, so replicates/instances machinery isn't expected to be needed.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "smoker", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "grill", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "burner", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "cooler", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "prep", "maxConcurrent": 2 }
  ],
  "actors": 2
}
```
